body:
The goal here is to have time series of numerical results for tracking progress.

---

From Claude: Pete asked me to open this so the AMIP leaderboard's numerical values are saved as data, which gives a time series of them across runs, and I wrote the change.

`compute_leaderboard` computes CliMA's global RMSE for each variable and season next to the CMIP6 models' RMSEs, but only saves them as `bias_leaderboard.png`, so there's no way to follow them across runs without reading the plot. This also writes `leaderboard_rmse.csv` next to the plot, one row per variable and season:

```
short_name,season,rmse,other_models_median_rmse,other_models_best_rmse,n_other_models,units
pr,ANN,1.5,2.0,1.0,40,"mm / day"
```

The median and best are over the other models only, not including CliMA. RMSEs that weren't computed are `NaN`. The variables are the ones with CMIP6 RMSEs to compare against: `pr`, `rsut`, and `rlut`.

The file lands in the job's `artifacts` directory, which the AMIP, long-run, and nightly pipelines already upload with `output/<run>/artifacts/*`, so it's uploaded as `output/<job_id>/artifacts/leaderboard_rmse.csv` with no pipeline changes. [clima-perf](https://github.com/petebachant/clima-perf) mirrors the weekly `climacoupler-amip` and `climacoupler-longruns` jobs, and will fetch this file to build a time series of each variable's RMSE alongside the CMIP6 median and best model. Nothing else changes; the plots are the same.

Testing: I ran `write_rmses` on a hand-built `RMSEVariable` with three models plus CliMA, including missing CliMA values and a `NaN` in another model, checked the medians and best values by hand, and read the file back with a CSV parser. I haven't run a full AMIP leaderboard locally. JuliaFormatter 2.10.1 makes no changes.

title: Write leaderboard RMSEs to a CSV artifact
